title: StockAgent architecture, as trees

steps.caption: StockAgent researches NSE stocks and trades them with paper money: data flows left to right, to a verdict, a trade and a message to you.
Every Saturday, discovery screens the market and analyses the best few; the ideas that pass wait on a shelf with an entry price band.
Research turns one stock into one verdict from a checked bundle of data; a gate can refuse to give one when too much is missing.
Portfolio applies written rules to hold, add, trim, sell or switch, and buys shelf ideas, in paper money at the reviewed day’s close.
Learning forecasts each managed stock for a month, grades it every weekday and reads the market’s mood; in production it changes no weights.
Measurement grades matured calls against the Nifty every night; the grades change no decision, and broken rules are reported to the owner.
From below: which module writes which file. The portfolio’s transaction ledger is the authority for every holding and trade.
The clock drives it all: at 16:30 on weekdays the review grades the previous session, then the portfolio trades at that session’s close.

steps.text: discovery: XYZ ranks high ─► deep dive: BUY by band and model, conviction 0.68, actionable
shelf (entry band, invalidation level) ─► ‘tracking only’ alert to all
paper envelope and weekly paper review start
reviews Friday ─► XYZ not offered (its dive came after Friday’s close)
reviews Monday ─► XYZ is a buy candidate; regime NORMAL, book below 80% ─► size 3.2% of equity
band, surveillance, identity, caps, cash floor all pass ─► BUY at Monday’s close; costs charged; case written; XYZ joins the managed list
its envelope is made by the next deploy’s self-heal, the 1st-of-month job or a manual trigger; until then ‘skipped: no_envelope’ and the advice reads a FLAT path: no ADD, price stops still protect it
16:30 grades its forecast row ─► advisor: HOLD / ADD / TRIM / EXIT / SWITCH
08:15 and 18:30 the events feed watches its filings and news
23:45 the auditor grades matured advice against the Nifty
for example a stop breach ─► EXIT ─► SELL at that session’s close ─► realised profit or loss ─► alert and digest ─► resale wait before it can be bought back
weekly results: the closed trade, its exit reason, the book against the Nifty
